The premiums are harder to justify from the available evidence:
• Ninja Premier, $599.99: its matched Best Buy page supports a 25-setting conical grinder, integrated scale, espresso, drip coffee and cold brew. Against the reported $449.99 Mini, the scale and conical grinder are shared benefits. Premier's hands-free frothing could improve preparation, but its page also describes manual frothing; dual capability is plausible and automatic operation remains unresolved. Cold brew adds versatility, with little direct benefit to your two morning milk drinks. I cannot establish better espresso, faster sequential drinks or easier cleaning sufficient to justify the extra $150.
• Breville Impress, $649.99: the matched Target page supports PID temperature control, a 25-setting conical grinder, 54mm portafilter, steam wand and 120 V operation.
